rows.text: Create a Python 3.12 application that prints "Hello, World!" when executed.
Organize the application as a small Python package with a main entry point.
Create a Python 3.12 CLI calculator.
It must support addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of two numbers.
Display the result on the command line.
Division by zero must produce a clear error message.
Create a Python 3.12 command-line todo application.
Users can add tasks, list tasks, mark a task as completed and delete a task.
Store the tasks in memory.
Create a Python 3.12 command-line todo application.
Users can add, list, complete and delete tasks.
Tasks must be stored in SQLite so that they remain available after restarting the application.
Create a Python 3.12 application for managing contacts.
A contact has a name, email address and phone number.
Provide operations to create, list, update and delete contacts.
Store the data in SQLite.
Create a Python 3.12 application for managing products.
Each product has a name, description, price and quantity.
Provide CRUD operations and persist the data in SQLite.
Create a Python 3.12 application for managing books.
Users can create, list, update and delete books.
Users must also be able to search books by title.
Persist the books in SQLite.
Create a Python 3.12 inventory application.
Products have a name, category, price and quantity.
Provide CRUD operations.
Users must be able to filter products by category and display products whose quantity is below a specified threshold.
Create a Python 3.12 application for managing employees.
An employee has a name, email address, age and salary.
The email must be valid, age must be between 18 and 70, and salary must be positive.
Provide CRUD operations using SQLite.
Create a Python 3.12 CLI application for managing notes.
Organize the code into separate modules for the data model, persistence, business logic and CLI.
Notes have a title, content and creation date.
Provide create, list, update and delete operations using SQLite.
Create a Python 3.12 library management application.
The application manages books with title, author, ISBN and publication year.
Users can create, list, update, search and delete books.
The ISBN must be unique.
Persist the data in SQLite.
Create a Python 3.12 customer management application.
Customers have a name, email and phone number.
Email addresses must be unique.
Provide CRUD operations, search by name and filtering by email domain.
Use SQLite persistence.
Create a Python 3.12 inventory application.
Products have a SKU, name, category, price and stock quantity.
SKUs must be unique.
Provide CRUD operations, product search, category filtering and low-stock reporting.
Create a Python 3.12 application for managing projects.
Projects have a name, description and status.
Users can create, update, list and delete projects.
Deleting a project must be implemented as a soft delete: the project remains in the database but is no longer returned by normal listing operations.
Create a Python 3.12 application for managing products.
Provide CRUD operations and allow users to list products sorted by name, price or quantity, in ascending or descending order.
Create a Python 3.12 application for managing customers.
Provide CRUD operations and a paginated listing operation.
The caller specifies page number and page size.
The application must return the requested items and enough information to determine the total number of pages.
Create a Python 3.12 inventory application.
Products have name, category, price and quantity.
Users must be able to search by name, filter by category, specify a maximum price and specify a minimum quantity.
All filters must be combinable.
Create a Python 3.12 contact management application using SQLite.
Provide normal CRUD operations and commands to export all contacts to CSV and import contacts from CSV.
Invalid rows during import must be rejected without corrupting existing data.
Create a Python 3.12 task management application using SQLite.
Provide CRUD operations and commands to export all tasks to JSON and import tasks from JSON.
The import operation must validate the input before modifying the database.
Create a Python 3.12 sales application.
Products and sales must be persisted in SQLite.
Provide CRUD operations for products and sales.
The application must also provide a report showing total sales amount and number of sales per product.
Create a Python 3.12 order management application.
Customers can have multiple orders.
Each order belongs to exactly one customer and has a date and status.
Provide CRUD operations for customers and orders and allow users to list all orders belonging to a customer.
Create a Python 3.12 order management application.
An order contains multiple products.
A product can appear in multiple orders.
Each order item contains a quantity and unit price.
Provide CRUD operations and calculate the total order amount.
Create a Python 3.12 blog management application.
Authors can create posts.
Each post belongs to one author and can have multiple tags.
A tag can be associated with multiple posts.
Provide CRUD operations for authors, posts and tags, and allow posts to be searched by tag.
Create a Python 3.12 project management application.
A project contains multiple tasks.
Each task belongs to one project and has a title, description, status and priority.
Users must be able to create, update, delete and list projects and tasks.
Create a Python 3.12 employee management application.
Employees belong to departments.
Each department can contain many employees.
Provide CRUD operations and allow users to list employees belonging to a department.
Create a Python 3.12 library application managing books, members and loans.
A member can borrow multiple books, but a book can have at most one active loan.
Users must be able to create and close loans and determine which books are currently available.
Create a Python 3.12 reservation application managing customers and rooms.
A customer can make multiple reservations.
A room cannot have two overlapping reservations.
Provide CRUD operations and reject reservations that overlap an existing reservation.
Create a Python 3.12 invoicing application.
An invoice belongs to a customer and contains multiple invoice lines.
Each line references a product and quantity.
The invoice total must be calculated from its lines.
Create a Python 3.12 application for managing customers and orders.
Organize the application into separate modules for models, repositories, services and CLI.
The service layer must contain the business rules and repositories must contain persistence logic.
Create a Python 3.12 task management application using a repository pattern.
The application must have a repository interface, a SQLite implementation and a service layer.
The CLI must use the service layer and must not access SQLite directly.
Create a Python 3.12 banking application managing customers and accounts.
An account belongs to a customer and has a balance.
Deposits increase the balance and withdrawals decrease it.
A withdrawal must be rejected if it would make the balance negative.

Create a Python 3.12 order management application. An order starts in the `pending` state and can become `confirmed`, `shipped` or `cancelled`. A cancelled order cannot be shipped, and a shipped order cannot be cancelled. Implement the allowed state transitions explicitly.
Create a Python 3.12 customer management application.
Provide CRUD operations for customers.
Every creation, update and deletion must also produce an audit record containing the operation, customer ID and timestamp.
Create a Python 3.12 order application.
Creating an order must create the order and all its order lines atomically.
If any order line is invalid, neither the order nor any of its lines should remain in the database.
Create a Python 3.12 inventory application.
Provide normal product CRUD operations and a bulk update operation that changes the stock quantity of multiple products.
The entire bulk update must succeed or fail as a single transaction.
Create a Python 3.12 application managing products and categories.
Every product must belong to an existing category.
A category cannot be deleted while products still belong to it.
Create a Python 3.12 project management application with projects and tasks.
Deleting a project must also remove its tasks.
The operation must be atomic.
Create a Python 3.12 CLI application managing users and documents.
Users must authenticate before accessing documents.
A user can only read, modify or delete their own documents.
Create a Python 3.12 application managing users, products and orders.
Administrators can manage products and users.
Normal users can create orders and view their own orders but cannot modify products or other users.
Create a Python 3.12 order application.
When an order is confirmed, the application must send a notification.
Define a notification service abstraction and provide a simple implementation that logs the notification instead of sending a real message.
Build a small application for managing a library.
Users should be able to manage books and members and keep track of loans.
The application should make it easy to know which books are available.
Create something to manage customers and their purchases.
Users should be able to find a customer's purchase history and determine how much they have spent.
Build a lightweight project management tool.
Projects contain tasks, tasks have priorities and statuses, and users should be able to see what needs attention.
Create an application for a small shop.
The shop needs to keep track of products, customers and sales.
It should be possible to know what has been sold and what is still in stock.
Build a simple booking system for a small hotel.
Staff should be able to manage rooms, guests and bookings and should not accidentally book the same room twice for the same period.
Create a small invoicing application for a freelance business.
It should keep track of clients, invoices and payments and make it possible to know which invoices are still outstanding.
Build a tool for managing a software team's work.
The team needs projects, tasks and people, and should be able to see who is responsible for what.
Create an application for managing a collection of books.
Users should be able to add books, find books and organize them.
The application should remember the information between executions.
Build an application for managing employees in a company.
Managers need to know which employees belong to which departments and should be able to find employees quickly.
Create a small application for managing events.
People should be able to create events and register for them.
The application should prevent registrations when an event is full.
Create a product management application.
Each product must have a unique SKU.
At the same time, the system must allow multiple products to use the same SKU when they belong to different categories.
Create a library management application where a book can be borrowed by members.
A book that is currently being borrowed should not appear as available.
When it is returned, it should become available again.
Create an order management application.
Customers can place orders containing products.
A customer must not be able to place an order if any product has insufficient stock.
When an order is successfully created, the corresponding stock quantities must be decreased.
Create an appointment application.
Appointments have a start and end time.
An appointment must always end after it starts, but the application must also support appointments whose start and end time are identical.
Create an inventory application.
Products have stock quantities.
Users can sell products.
The application should never allow the inventory to become incorrect.
Create a Python 3.12 CLI application for managing customers, orders and products.

Customers can have many orders, orders contain products, products have stock quantities, products can be searched and filtered, orders can be cancelled, cancelling an order must restore its product quantities, and all modifications must be persisted atomically in SQLite.
Create a Python 3.12 application for managing documents.
The CLI should remain independent from persistence so that the persistence mechanism can later be replaced without changing the business logic.
Create a Python 3.12 application that manages customers and retrieves additional customer information from an external service.
The application should continue to operate correctly when the external service is unavailable.
Create a simple Python 3.12 application for managing orders.
It should support customers, products, stock, orders, order lines, discounts, taxes, order cancellation, stock restoration, reporting and CSV export.
Keep the application easy to maintain and split it into appropriate modules.
Build a Python 3.12 application for a small business that manages customers, products, orders and invoices.
Customers can place orders containing multiple products.
Products belong to categories and have stock quantities.
Orders can be pending, confirmed, shipped or cancelled.
Confirming an order reserves stock.
Cancelling a confirmed order releases the reserved stock.
An invoice is created when an order is confirmed.
Customers should be able to search their orders and invoices.
Administrators should be able to manage products and categories.

The application must persist all data in SQLite, expose the main operations through a CLI, validate input, handle errors cleanly, keep business logic separate from persistence and remain reasonably modular.
Create a CLI tool that reads a CSV file and outputs JSON.
The tool should accept the input file path and an optional output file path.
If no output path is given, print to stdout.
Include error handling for missing files and malformed CSV.
CRITICAL: Read the CSV header row to determine column names dynamically.
Do NOT assume specific column names like "title" or "name".
Convert each row to a JSON object using the actual headers as keys.
**Category model** — id, name (unique), description, monthly_budget (optional int, stored as cents), icon (optional str)
**Expense model** — id, amount_cents (int), description, expense_date (str, ISO date), category_id (FK), payment_method (cash/card/transfer), is_recurring (bool)
**Budget model** — id, category_id (FK), month (str like "2024-01"), amount_limit_cents (int), UNIQUE(category_id, month)
→ DDL: use table-level `UNIQUE(category_id, month)`, not inline `month TEXT UNIQUE`
**ExpenseRepository** — SQLite storage with CRUD + filtering by date range, category, payment_method + monthly/yearly aggregation queries
**CategoryRepository** — SQLite storage with CRUD + find expenses for a category
**BudgetRepository** — SQLite storage with CRUD + find budgets by month + check if a category has exceeded its budget

list_expenses(category_id (Optional[int]), start_date (Optional[date]), end_date (Optional[date]), payment_method (Optional[str])): lists expenses filtered by optional category, date range, payment method — all params are optional, so passing no filters returns all expenses
get_expense_by_id(id): returns a single expense by its ID
add_expense: validates category exists, adds expense, checks if budget exceeded after insertion
update_expense(id, data): updates an expense's fields
delete_expense(id): deletes an expense by ID
get_monthly_report(month): returns total spent, per-category breakdown, budget status (on_track/warning/exceeded) for a given "YYYY-MM" month
get_yearly_summary(year): returns monthly totals, top spending categories, average monthly spend
get_category_spending(category_id, start_date, end_date): returns aggregated spending for a category over a period
export_to_csv(file_path, start_date, end_date): exports filtered expenses as CSV
detect_recurring(): finds expenses with same amount/category recurring monthly and marks them

`expense category list`

Use type hints throughout.
Use SQLite with foreign keys enabled.
All monetary values must be stored as integers (cents) to avoid floating-point precision issues — convert to/from decimal for display.
All IDs must be auto-incremented primary keys that are optional (default None) in the domain models.
Implement proper error handling with custom exception classes: CategoryNotFoundError, ExpenseNotFoundError, BudgetExceededException.
Build a Python 3.12 application for a local wine shop owner to manage their premium wine inventory and tracks bottle storage locations.
Provide a responsive GUI (Graphical User Interface) for the shop owner to visually manage the bottles, update stock levels, and assign bottles to physical locations (e.g., Rack A, Shelf 3).
The application must persist all data locally across sessions.
Enforce a strict separation between the visual presentation layer, the data persistence access layer, and the core domain logic.
Wine Model: unique identifier, name, vintage year (int), wine type (red, white, rosé, sparkling), country of origin, cost price, selling price, and total current stock quantity.
Storage Location Model: unique identifier, zone name (e.g., "Main Cellar", "Front Display"), row number, shelf number, and maximum bottle capacity.
Each wine bottle entry must point to exactly one primary storage location.
The selling price of a wine bottle must always be strictly greater than its cost price.
A wine's stock quantity can never drop below zero.
The total number of bottles assigned to a specific storage location cannot exceed that location's defined maximum bottle capacity.
All wine names must be unique in the system.
Prevent the removal of a storage location if wine bottles are currently assigned to it.
Implement clean user validation with intuitive error handling.
Raise custom domain exceptions when business constraints are violated, such as NegativeStockError, LocationOverCapacityException, or InvalidPricingException.
Create a simple Python script with a CLI entry point that prints "Hello, World!" with type hints.
The script should define a `main()` function and include the standard `if __name__ == "__main__": main()` guard.

**Product model** — id, sku (unique), name, category_id (FK), price_cents (int), stock_qty (int), low_active (optional bool, default False, whether the product is still sold)
**CategoryRepository** — SQLite storage with CRUD + find all products belonging to a category
**ProductRepository** — SQLite storage with CRUD + find products by category + find low-stock products (stock_qty below reorder_threshold) + aggregate total stock value by category

update_product(id, data): updates a product's fields
delete_product(id): deletes a product by ID
get_product_by_id(id): returns a single product by its ID

restock(id, qty): increases a product's stock_qty

Use type hints throughout.
Use SQLite with foreign keys enabled.
The database schema must enforce referential integrity with CASCADE deletes.
Follow clean architecture with proper separation of concerns.
All IDs must be auto-incremented primary keys that are optional (default None) in the domain models.
Every `Book` has exactly one required `author_id: int` foreign key to `Author.id`. Deleting an author cascades to that author's books; deleting a book cascades to its loans.
Add `library author add --name --birth-year [--biography]` so the CLI can create an author before a book. `--biography` is optional text.
`library book add --author-id` requires an integer author ID. `--copies` is optional and defaults to one. `library book list --author` accepts an integer author ID and filters on `Book.author_id`.
`--available-only` is a no-value boolean flag. When present, it returns books with at least one available copy; when absent, it does not filter by copy count.

`library book search --query` performs case-insensitive substring matching across book title, author name, and ISBN. Return each book once even if multiple fields match. An ISBN miss returns an empty list.
`Member.membership_date` defaults to today's date when a member is created, so `library member add --name --email` is sufficient. New members start active.

A new loan is due 14 calendar days after its loan date. `LibraryService` computes the due date from a date value and passes it to the repository; the repository must not derive dates from `published_year`.
Zero available copies is valid. Reject only negative copy counts. Borrowing the final copy leaves the count at zero.

A loan is overdue when `due_date < today` and `return_date is None`. A late loan may still be returned. Returning sets `return_date` to today, sets status to `returned`, and restores exactly one available copy.
Returning an already returned loan raises `AlreadyReturnedLoanError` and changes neither the loan nor inventory. Include that error in the declared error set.
Without a background scheduler, report overdue status as a derived read result while the stored status remains `active` until the loan is returned.
Borrowing and returning each perform all related writes in one SQLite transaction. If any write fails, roll back every write in that operation.
When an ID field defaults to `None`, annotate it `int | None`. Preserve SQLite auto-increment for IDs and enforce the declared unique ISBN and email constraints.
